sources.citation: Melis et al. (2014), A VLBI Resolution of the Pleiades Distance Controversy
Pinned common ICRS image-frame origin derived from registered observations; adopted display centre, not a measured nebular centroid.

introduction.text: The Pleiades is an open star cluster surrounded by reflection nebulosity. Its stars lie about 136 parsecs away; the dust may not.

distance.method: Adopted VLBI stellar-cluster distance from Melis et al. (2014), main text and Table 1; not a measured distance to each dust filament.

subject.name: Pleiades stellar cluster
subject.reason: The stellar-cluster distance locates the reflection-nebula scene; individual dust-filament distances are not measured.

classification.name: Reflection nebula around an open cluster
classification.basis: Observed optical reflection nebulosity and infrared dust emission painted on an authored finite depth surface. The stellar distance locates the scene; dust depth, scattering and individual stellar distances are not recovered.
